answer: Require each agent to post a bond that can be slashed when its claims fail a randomly sampled, independently verified task. To earn rewards, identities must also accumulate a history of useful work; splitting effort across fresh accounts resets that history and ties up more capital. At dawn, a jade marketplace might admit newcomers, but only bonded, proven agents gain influence by zenith. A sybil attacker must fund many bonds and sustain credible work, making cheap identity multiplication costly rather than automatically persuasive.
